text:
Predicates:
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
RequiresDeposit(x) ::: x requires a deposit to rent an apartment.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: x has a security deposit amount y.
MonthlyRent(x, y) ::: x has a monthly rent amount y.
MoreThan(x, y) ::: x is more than y.
Owns(x, y) ::: x owns y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
AllowsPets(x) ::: x allows pets.
AllowedToMoveInWith(x, y, z) ::: x is allowed to move into y with z.
RentApartment(x, y) ::: x will rent an apartment in y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ AllowsPets(x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → RequiresDeposit(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → ∃y (SecurityDeposit(x, y) ∧ (y = MonthlyRent(x, y) ∨ MoreThan(y, MonthlyRent(x, y))))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to the monthly rent at a managed building or more.
Owns(tom, fluffy) ∧ Cat(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
MoreThan(2000, 1500) ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
(AllowedToMoveInWith(tom, oliveGarden, fluffy) ∧ SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, y) ∧ ¬MoreThan(y, 1500)) → RentApartment(tom, oliveGarden) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
∀x ∀y (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ AllowsPets(x) → AllowedToMoveInWith(y, x, z) ∧ Pet(z)) ::: If a managed building allows pets, then people are allowed to move in with a pet.
Conclusion:
AllowedToMoveInWith(tom, oliveGarden, fluffy) ::: Tom is allowed to move into an apartment in The Olive Garden with Fluffy.
